name: Spearfish heavyweight torpedo
overview_md:
The Spearfish is the Royal Navy's heavyweight submarine-launched torpedo and one of the fastest in the world — the weapon of Britain's Astute- and Trafalgar-class attack submarines and Vanguard-class ballistic-missile boats. Its inclusion in an Indo-Pacific reference reflects the AUKUS partnership and Britain's "tilt" to the region: UK submarines now deploy east of Suez, and Australia's future SSN-AUKUS boats draw on a shared Anglo-American undersea ecosystem.

Spearfish's distinguishing trait is raw speed. Powered by a Sundstrand 21TP04 gas-turbine engine running on Otto fuel and HAP-Othol oxidiser, it can reach speeds reported above 80 knots — significantly faster than most heavyweight torpedoes — letting it run down fast nuclear submarines and high-speed surface ships. It is wire-guided with active and passive sonar homing and a directed-energy warhead designed to defeat double-hulled submarines.

The definitive Spearfish Mod 1 upgrade, now in service, adds a fibre-optic guidance link (replacing copper wire) for far higher-bandwidth two-way communication, an insensitive-munition warhead for safer handling, and improved processing for cluttered littoral waters. For an analyst, Spearfish rounds out the picture of allied undersea firepower in the Pacific — alongside the U.S. Mk 48 and Japan's Type 89 — as the West leans on its submarine advantage to offset China's surface and missile mass.

variants_json.name: Spearfish Mod 1
variants_json.key_changes: Fibre-optic link, insensitive-munition warhead, improved processing

combat_history.event: No combat employment; the Royal Navy's standard submarine heavyweight torpedo, demonstrated in SINKEX.
combat_history.significance: Unproven in war but technically among the fastest torpedoes fielded.

modernization.description: Fibre-optic guidance and insensitive-munition warhead across the fleet.

vulnerabilities.description: Very high speed comes at some cost to range and noise.
vulnerabilities.context: Fast runs are louder and shorter than economical settings.

vulnerabilities.description: Must defeat modern decoys and jammers in terminal homing.
vulnerabilities.context: Quiet peer submarines stress the seeker.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Anti-submarine and anti-surface engagements from Royal Navy submarines, increasingly deploying to the Indo-Pacific.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Astute/Trafalgar SSNs; Vanguard SSBNs for self-defence.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Mod 1 in service; AUKUS commonality growing.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The Mk 48 is more widely fielded with broadband CBASS sonar; Spearfish is notably faster.
Comparable heavyweight role in the allied undersea force.
China's heavyweight torpedo, the undersea threat AUKUS boats would face.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: The West's undersea edge vs China.

doctrine.role: Royal Navy submarine-launched heavyweight torpedo emphasising very high speed.
doctrine.employment: Wire/fibre-optic guided with sonar terminal homing; runs down fast submarines and surface ships.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Speed above all — outrun and overtake high-performance targets.
doctrine.threat_context: Part of allied undersea firepower projecting into the Pacific under AUKUS.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the Mk 48 (US), Type 89 (Japan) and China's Yu-6.
